questions.question: Who founded the independent State of Bengal?
questions.solution:
• Murshid Quli Khan (Zamin Ali Quli, born as Surya Narayan Mishra) was the first Nawab of Bengal (1717 to 1727) and founded the independent state of Bengal.
  • He built the Katra Masjid (1723-1724), where he was buried after his death.

questions.question: Who among the following was the Maharana of Mewar and composed a book on music called 'Sangeet Raj'?
questions.solution:
• Maharana Kumbha (1433-1468 AD) of the Sisodia clan composed 'Sangeet Raj'.
  • His titles included Abhinav Bhattacharya, Rajguru, Daanguru, Halguru, and Rano Raso.

questions.question: Name the Bhakti Saint from South India who was initially a Jaina and a minister in the court of a Chalukya king in the twelfth century.
questions.solution:
• Basavanna was the Bhakti saint from South India who was initially a Jaina and a minister in the court of Kalachurya king Bijjala (1157-1167).
  • He was the founder of Lingayatism and founded the Anubhava Mantapa.

questions.question: The eleventh century structure of Bhojshala in the state of Madhya Pradesh was constructed under the patronage of which dynasty?
questions.solution:
• Bhojshala (the only temple of Mata Saraswati) in Dhar district, Madhya Pradesh, was constructed under the patronage of the Paramara dynasty.
  • The Paramara dynasty ruled Malwa from the 9th to the 14th century. Founder: Upendra or Krishnaraja.

questions.question: In which of the following places is the Tomb of Ahmad Shah Al Wali Bahmani built?
questions.solution:
• The Tomb of Ahmad Shah Al Wali Bahmani (Bahmani Sultanate, 1422 to 1436) is built at Ashtoor.
  • Ashtoor is an important center of Indo-Saracenic monuments east of Bidar, with twelve imposing mausoleums.

questions.question: The Hoyasleshvara temple was built with which of the following stones by a Hoyasla king in 1150?
questions.solution:
• The Hoyasleshvara temple was built with Dark Schist Stone by a Hoyasla king in 1150.
  • The temples were known for their pillared hall and stellated plan.
  • The capital of the Hoyasla dynasty was Dorasamudra (Dwarasamudra).

questions.question: Udaipur was founded by ______ after the fall of Chittor to Akbar in 1568.
questions.solution:
• Udaipur was founded by Rana Uda Singh after the fall of Chittor to Akbar in 1568.
  • Udaipur is known as the 'Venice of the East' and the city of lakes.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Indian architectural styles:
1. The use of overhanging balconies and arched cornices is a distinctive feature of Mughal architecture.
2. The Rajput fort 'Hawa Mahal' in Jaipur is an example of Rajput architecture, built by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
• Statement 1 is incorrect: Overhanging balconies and arched cornices belong to Rajput architecture, not Mughal.
  • Statement 2 is correct: Hawa Mahal in Jaipur is an example of Rajput architecture, built by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh.

questions.question: Ananga Pala was a ruler of which dynasty?
questions.solution:
• Ananga Pala was a ruler of the Rajput Dynasty (Tomara dynasty), ruling over areas of Delhi.
  • The Rajput Dynasty was founded by Simharaj, who is famously known as the founder of the city of Ajmer.

questions.question: The Ahom Kingdom in India was located in the
questions.solution:
• The Ahom Kingdom was located in the Brahmaputra valley.
  • Chaolung Sukapha founded the Ahom kingdom (13th century) that ruled Assam for six centuries.
  • It was annexed by British India in 1826 with the signing of the Treaty of Yandaboo.
  • Lachit Borphukan (military general of the Ahom kingdom) defeated Mughal forces in the Battle of Saraighat (1671).

questions.question: What did the medieval term 'Raqs' mean?
questions.solution:
• The medieval term 'Raqs' meant dancing.
  • Other medieval terms: Amils (Revenue), Bargir (Cavalrymen), Daam (Coin), Dhimmis (Non-Muslims people), Din (Religion), Diwan (Function of finance), Wilayat (The spiritual territory of a Sufi).

questions.question: Bhakti saints, Nayanars were devotees of which of the following gods?
questions.solution:
• The Nayanars were a group of 63 saints devoted to Lord Shiva, who lived during the 6th to 8th centuries CE.
  • The Alwars were Tamil poet-saints of South India who espoused devotion to Lord Vishnu.

questions.question: Which among the following forts was the principal capital of Qutb Shahi dynasty in Hyderabad?
questions.solution:
• Golconda Fort was the principal capital of the Qutb Shahi dynasty in Hyderabad. It was built by the Kakatiya Dynasty.
  • Rajgad Fort (Pune, Maharashtra) was renovated by Chhatrapati Shivaji and made his capital in 1674 AD.
  • Chiktan Fort is in Kargil (Ladakh).

questions.question: Which of the following books was written by the Roman writer Pliny the elder?
questions.solution:
• Pliny the Elder wrote 'Natural History'.
  • Important books and authors: Gathasaptashati - Hala, Indica - Megasthenes, Geographica - Strabo, Periplus of the Erythraean Sea - William H Schoff, Kathasaritsagara - Somadeva, Mudrarakshasa - Vishakhadatta, Rajtarangini - Kalhana.

questions.question: Which of the following cities became the capital of Bengal in 1704?
questions.solution:
• Murshidabad became the capital of Bengal in 1704 AD.
  • Murshid Quli Khan (Zamin Ali Quli) transferred his capital to Makhsudabad, later renamed Murshidabad after him.
  • Murshidabad (West Bengal) on the banks of the Bhagirathi became the center of silk.
  • Murshid Quli Khan (1717-1727) was the first Nawab of Bengal.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement is correct with respect to the Prashastis and land grants?
I. Prashastis were composed by learned Brahmanas.
II. Kings often rewarded Brahmanas by grants of land which were recorded on copper plates.
questions.solution:
• Both statements I and II are correct.
  • Prashastis (metal plates) were written by Brahmanas in Sanskrit or regional languages in prose or poetry form.
  • Example: Allahabad Pillar Inscription (Sanskrit poem by Harishena in praise of King Samudragupta).
  • Agrahara (Agraharam, Ghatoka, Boya) refers to land/village given to Brahmanas.

questions.question: The craftspersons of Bidar were so famed for their inlay work in
questions.solution:
• The craftspersons of Bidar (Karnataka) were famed for their inlay work in copper and silver, called Bidri.
  • Bidar was the capital of the Bahmani Kingdom in the 14th century.
  • Bidar fort was built by Ahmad Shah Wali Bahman.
  • Bidar is also considered one of the holiest places for Sikh pilgrimage.

questions.question: In 1342, one of the nobles, Haji Ilyas Khan united Bengal and became its ruler under the title of ______ and laid the foundation of the Ilyas Shah dynasty.
questions.solution:
• Shams-ud-din Ilyas Shah was the founder of the Bengal Sultanate and the Ilyas Shahi dynasty (first dynasty of Bengal).
  • Dynasties of Bengal Sultanate: Ilyas Shahi (1342-1415), Ganesha (1414-1435), Restorer of Ilyas Dynasty (Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah I, 1435-1487), Habshi rule (Shahzada Barbak, 1487-1494), and Hussain Shahi dynasty (Alauddin Hussain Shah, 1494-1519).

questions.question: Who was the architect of the famous Mysore Palace in Karnataka?
questions.solution:
• Henry Irwin was the architect of the famous Mysore Palace (also known as Amba Villas) in Karnataka.
  • It was the official residence of the Wadiyar dynasty.
  • Mysore Palace was constructed in Indo-Saracenic style architecture.

questions.question: The Vimana in the Dravidian style of temple architecture is usually in which shape?
questions.solution:
• The Vimana in Dravidian temple architecture is usually pyramidal in shape.
  • Gopuram is the entrance gateway in the center of the front wall.
  • Antarala is the vestibular tunnel; garbhagriha is the innermost sanctuary.
  • Famous Dravidian Temples: Rajarajeswara/Brihadeshwara temple (Thanjavur), Gangaikondacholapuram temple, Annamalaiyar Temple (Tiruvannamalai), Meenakshi Temple, Airavatesvara Temple.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about a fort:
1. It was originally known as Mankal.
2. It was built on a hilltop in 1143.
In the above mentioned sentences, which fort is being talked about?
questions.solution:
• Golconda Fort (Hyderabad) was originally known as Mankal and was built on a hilltop in 1143 by the Qutb Shahi dynasty.
  • Chitradurga Fort (Karnataka) was built by the Chalukyas and Hoysalas.
  • Daulatabad Fort (Maharashtra) was built by the Yadava dynasty.
  • Aguada Fort (Goa) was built by the Portuguese.

questions.question: The ancient Neemrana Baori is located in which of the following districts of Rajasthan?
questions.solution:
• The ancient Neemrana Baori is located in Alwar district of Rajasthan.
  • Famous Baoris in India: Chand Baori (Rajasthan), Agrasen Ki Baoli (New Delhi), Rani ki Vav (Gujarat), Pushkarani (Karnataka), Baoli Ghaus Ali Shah (Haryana), Mata Bhavani ni Vav (Gujarat), Rajon ki Baoli (New Delhi), Surya Kund (Gujarat).

questions.question: Who among the following was given the title of 'Uttarapatha Swamin'?
questions.solution:
• Dharmapala assumed the title of 'Uttarapatha Swamin', along with Parama Bhattaraka, Paramesvara, and Maharajadhiraja.
  • He was the successor of Gopala (founder of the Pala empire).
  • He was a pious Buddhist and founded Vikramshila University in Bhagalpur, Bihar.

questions.question: Who was the ruler of Mysore in 1761?
questions.solution:
• Hyder Ali was the ruler of Mysore in 1761.
  • In 1769, he defeated the British forces several times and reached the Madras walls.
  • In the Second Anglo-Mysore War, he died in 1782 and was succeeded by his son Tipu Sultan.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. The book 'Man Kautuha' was compiled by Raja Mansingh Tomar.
2. Raja Mansingh Tomar was the ruler of Gwalior.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
• Both statements 1 and 2 are correct.
  • Raja Mansingh Tomar, ruler of Gwalior, compiled the book 'Man Kautuha'.
